definitions.text: Work is defined as the product of magnitude of force and the distance covered in the direction of force.
One joule work is done when a force of one newton acting on a body moves it through a distance of one metre in its own direction.
Energy can be defined as the ability of a body to do work.
The kinetic energy of a body is the energy that a body possesses by virtue of its motion.
Potential energy is defined as the energy that a body possesses by virtue of its position or deformation.
the energy possessed by an object by virtue of its position relative to the Earth is known as gravitational potential energy.
The energy stored in a compressed or stretched spring is called elastic potential energy
Energy cannot be created or destroyed. It may be transformed from one form to another, but the total amount of energy never changes.
Fossil fuel energy is the energy that is released by burning of oil, coal and natural gas.
Hydroelectric generation is the electricity generated by using the kinetic energy of the falling water.
Solar energy is the energy of the sunlight that can be converted into electricity.
The energy released by breaking the nucleus of an atom is known as nuclear energy.
Geothermal energy is the heat energy of the hot rocks present deep under the surface of the Earth.
Wind energy is the electrical energy produced by using the kinetic energy of the fast-blowing wind.
Biofuel energy is that energy which is obtained by fermentation of organic materials in the form of biogas or ethanol.
The resources of energy which are replaced by new ones after their use are called renewable energy source.
On the other hand, non-renewable sources are those, which are depleted with the continuous use.
Power is defined as the time rate of doing work.
One watt is the work done at the rate of one joule per second.
The ratio of useful output energy and the total input energy is called the efficiency of a working system.
It is a hypothetical machine that can do work indefinitely, without any external source of energy.

formulas.use: Work when force and displacement are in the same direction (W in J, F in N, S in m).
Work when the force makes an angle with the displacement (W in J, F in N, S in m, θ in rad).

formulas.formula: W = area under the force–distance graph
formulas.use: Work done by a force from its force–distance graph (W in J; force in N; distance in m).
Convert between joules and newton metres (J in joules, N in newtons, m in metres).
Convert kilojoules or megajoules to joules (all energy values in J, kJ, or MJ).
Find force from mass and acceleration, including in kinetic-energy problems (F in N, m in kg, a in m s⁻²).
Find the magnitude of acceleration when velocity changes by v in time t, as in the stopping-body derivation (a in m s⁻², v in m s⁻¹, t in s).
Distance while slowing uniformly from speed v to rest (S in m, v in m s⁻¹, t in s).
Kinetic energy of a moving body (Eₖ and W in J, m in kg, v in m s⁻¹).

formulas.formula: Eₚ = W = F × h = m × g × h
formulas.use: Gravitational potential energy gained by lifting a body (Eₚ and W in J, F in N, h in m, m in kg, g in m s⁻²).
Total mechanical energy when energy changes between potential and kinetic forms without losses (Eₚ and Eₖ in J).

formulas.formula: Eₚ = m × g × (h − x); Eₖ = m × g × x; Eₚ + Eₖ = m × g × h
formulas.use: Energy of a falling body at a point x above the ground, neglecting air resistance (all energies in J, m in kg, g in m s⁻², h and x in m).
Power from work done over time (P in W, work W in J, t in s).
Power from energy transferred over time (P in W, E in J, t in s).

formulas.formula: 1 W = 1 J ÷ 1 s; 1 kW = 10³ W; 1 MW = 10⁶ W; 1 hp = 746 W
formulas.use: Define or convert power units (W in watts, J in joules, s in seconds, hp in horsepower).

formulas.formula: Efficiency = useful output energy ÷ total input energy
formulas.use: Efficiency as a ratio (both energies in J; efficiency has no unit).

formulas.formula: Percentage efficiency = (useful output energy ÷ total input energy) × 100%
formulas.use: Efficiency as a percentage (both energies in J; percentage efficiency in %).

formulas.formula: Percentage efficiency = (useful power output ÷ total power input) × 100%
formulas.use: Efficiency using power values (both powers in W; percentage efficiency in %).

fullMarks: For a work question, write the given force, displacement and angle first; choose W = F × S × cos θ and show the component of force along the displacement if an angle is involved.
For every numerical, write the given data in SI units, the formula, substitution with units, and the final answer with its unit and sensible significant figures.
Convert mass to kilograms and speed to m s⁻¹ before using energy formulas; use the value of g given in the question, or state the value used.
For kinetic energy or potential energy, name the energy being calculated and show the formula before substituting values.

For energy-conservation questions, state that total energy remains constant, then describe which form decreases and which form increases at each position; label heights and energy forms clearly in a diagram.
For efficiency, show useful output energy and total input energy separately before dividing; multiply by 100% only when the question asks for percentage efficiency.
For a theory answer, start with the exact definition or law, then add the requested explanation or example; finish with the correct SI unit when a unit is asked for.
mistakes: Using W = F × S when the force is at an angle. Fix: use W = F × S × cos θ and include only the force component along the displacement.
Saying work is done just because a force is applied. Fix: check that the object has displacement in the direction of the force; if there is no displacement, work is zero.
Using speed in km h⁻¹ or mass in grams in an energy formula. Fix: convert speed to m s⁻¹ and mass to kg first.
Forgetting to square the speed in Eₖ = ½mv². Fix: square the speed before multiplying by mass and one-half.
Using the full ramp length instead of the vertical height to calculate gravitational potential energy. Fix: use Eₚ = mgh, where h is the vertical height gained.
Calculating efficiency as input divided by output, or forgetting × 100%. Fix: use useful output ÷ total input, then multiply by 100 for percentage efficiency.
Writing that energy disappears during a fall or collision. Fix: explain its transformation or transfer, including energy dissipated to the surroundings as heat or sound.
